subject: Human Evolution
title: Toolmaking and Language
description: A quick, practical guide to Toolmaking and Language.

hook.text: Brain scans show stone-knapping activates Broca's area—the same region that controls speech.

buildup.text: Both skills share a need for complex sequences: strike A, then B, then C in the right order.

discovery.text: Dietrich Stout argues that toolmaking may have paved neural pathways that language later borrowed.

twist.text: It's also possible language came first and enabled teaching complex tool recipes. Causation is debated.

climax.text: Either way, tools and language co-evolved—each pushing the other toward greater complexity.

quiz.question: What brain region is activated by both toolmaking and language?
